rad.5.coronary-ct.overview: Use coronary CT angiography to describe anatomy, stenosis, total plaque burden and any available physiology. Read the linked Radiology Assistant chapters alongside the original CAD-RADS 2.0 consensus. The structured report below expands the supplied CCTA example and keeps image quality, segment findings and classification together.
learning_points: Follow each artery from its ostium to the distal evaluable branches, reviewing source images alongside multiplanar reconstructions.
Explain the limitation when an apparently important narrowing may reflect motion, calcification or stent artefact.
Keep plaque burden, lumen narrowing and physiological significance as separate observations before integrating the impression.
Use the key-image checklist to make the dominant finding and its anatomical context easy to review.

sections.heading: CAD-RADS 2.0
sections.body:
CAD-RADS category:
0: no plaque or stenosis.
1: 1–24% stenosis, or plaque with positive remodelling but no luminal narrowing.
2: 25–49%.
3: 50–69%.
4A: 70–99% in one or two vessels.
4B: LM ≥50% or severe three-vessel disease.
5: total occlusion.
N: non-diagnostic.
Final CAD-RADS: CAD-RADS [0/1/2/3/4A/4B/5/N] / [P1/P2/P3/P4 when applicable] / [N / HRP / I+ / I− / I± / S / G / E as applicable].
If a relevant segment >1.5 mm is non-evaluable and evaluable segments show only <50% stenosis, use category N. If ≥50% stenosis is demonstrated elsewhere, retain the stenosis category and append N. Report P only if reliable.

sections.heading: IMPRESSION
sections.body:
1. [Right / left / co-dominant] coronary circulation.
2. Coronary origins/course: [normal / anomaly described].
3. CAD: [none / minimal / mild / moderate / severe / obstructive]. Most significant lesion: [vessel/segment], [plaque type], [stenosis category/%].
4. Plaque burden: [no plaque / P1 / P2 / P3 / P4 / indeterminate]. HRP: [absent / present].
5. Stents/grafts: [none / findings].
6. CAD-RADS 2.0: CAD-RADS [ ] / [P category if applicable] / [modifiers]. Physiology, if performed: [ ].
7. Non-coronary findings: [none significant / specify].
8. Diagnostic limitation affecting interpretation, if any: [ ].

sections.heading: OPTIONAL MANAGEMENT LINE
sections.body:
Clinical setting: [stable / acute chest pain / other]. Suggested next step: [ ], considering symptoms, ECG/troponin where relevant, prior treatment, comorbidity and patient preference.
Stable chest pain prompts: [0: usually no additional CAD testing / 1–2: preventive risk discussion / 3: consider functional assessment / 4A: consider ICA or functional assessment / 4B: consider ICA / 5: consider ICA with viability/functional assessment where appropriate / N: additional evaluation if clinically indicated].
Acute chest pain prompt: [integrate stenosis and image quality with the ACS pathway; do not diagnose or exclude ACS from CAD-RADS alone].
Document the individualised recommendation and rationale; delete unused options.

notes: Complete bracketed fields and remove unused alternatives before issuing a report. Use the study’s own de-identified images in the final report; the gallery contains independent published teaching examples.
The user-supplied CCTA example provides the report foundation. Classification clarifications are referenced to CAD-RADS 2.0.
S and G record the presence of stents and bypass grafts. E identifies a relevant non-atherosclerotic coronary exception that requires a narrative description.
A fixed perfusion defect should be described separately from reversible ischaemia. Record failed or non-diagnostic physiology explicitly.

rad.5.prostate-mri.overview: A prostate MRI report should connect the clinical question, examination quality, lesion map and local extent. Use the Radiology Assistant chapter for illustrated learning and ACR PI-RADS v2.1 for formal scoring. This original worksheet provides the reporting structure and image checklist.
learning_points: Identify the lesion's zone of origin before scoring and correlate the same location across T2, ADC, high-b-value DWI and DCE.
Describe BPH, inflammation and haemorrhage when they explain an apparent lesion or reduce confidence.
Keep PI-RADS suspicion separate from extension/staging findings, PSA density and subsequent management.
Use consistent lesion numbers, sector labels and image references so that comparison and biopsy targeting remain reproducible.

sections.heading: LESION WORKSHEET — REPEAT FOR EACH REPORTED LESION
sections.body:
Lesion [number]; index [yes/no].
Location [side, base/mid/apex, zone and sector(s)].
Size [ ] mm; sequence/plane [ ]; series/image [ ].
T2 appearance [ ]; score [1–5].
ADC/high-b DWI appearance [ ]; DWI score [1–5].
DCE [positive / negative / not assessable / not acquired].
Margin contact [ ]; extension [ ].
Overall PI-RADS [1–5]; scoring rationale [ ].
Comparison change [ ].

sections.heading: SCORING CHECK
sections.body:
PZ: DWI determines the category; DWI 3 becomes PI-RADS 4 only with positive DCE. Positive DCE requires focal early enhancement corresponding to the suspicious finding.
TZ: T2 determines the category, except T2 2 with DWI ≥4 becomes PI-RADS 3, and T2 3 with DWI 5 becomes PI-RADS 4. DCE does not upgrade TZ lesions.
A score-4-pattern lesion is score 5 on the relevant sequence at ≥1.5 cm or with definite extraprostatic extension/invasion.
No DCE means no DCE-based upgrade. If DWI is inadequate, consult the PI-RADS alternative-assessment table and state the limitation.

sections.heading: LOCAL EXTENT
sections.body:
Extraprostatic extension [absent / equivocal / present: site and evidence].
Neurovascular bundles [ ]; seminal vesicles [ ]; bladder neck [ ]; external sphincter [ ]; adjacent organs [ ].
MRI local-stage assessment when applicable [ ].

sections.heading: NODES / BONES / OTHER PELVIC FINDINGS
sections.body:
Suspicious nodes [none / station, short axis and morphology].
Bones within coverage [ ]. Other pelvic findings [ ].

sections.heading: IMPRESSION
sections.body:
1. Index lesion [site, size], PI-RADS [ ]; additional lesions [ ].
2. Local extension [ ]; suspicious nodes/bone findings [ ].
3. Volume [ ] mL; PSA density [ ].
4. Comparison and material limitation [ ].
5. Individualised next-step discussion, if appropriate [ ].

notes: PI-RADS categories express imaging suspicion: 1 very low; 2 low; 3 equivocal; 4 high; 5 very high likelihood of clinically significant cancer. They do not independently prescribe biopsy or treatment.
Choose the index lesion by highest PI-RADS category; resolve ties by extraprostatic extension, then size. Map up to four principal suspicious lesions and identify all sectors involved.
Measure AP and longitudinal gland dimensions on mid-sagittal T2, transverse on axial T2. Avoid mixing millimetres and centimetres in the ellipsoid formula.
PI-RADS diagnostic scoring is not a post-treatment recurrence system. A negative MRI does not exclude clinically significant cancer; interpret with clinical risk.
If both DWI and DCE are unavailable or inadequate, do not imply a complete PI-RADS assessment; the formal guidance limits assessment to staging for extraprostatic extension.
Use actual study images in the image slots and retain matching series/image references in the report.
